D015-D005_h024.question:
For the last couple of years things have really come apart. About eight months ago I dropped into this… pit. I was crying all the time, even in the edit bay over nothing, or in the car on the way home. I’d lie in bed for hours just staring at the ceiling, unable to fall asleep, and then drag myself through the day with no interest in food — some days I’d realize at night I’d only had a coffee and a granola bar. I felt absolutely certain that my films had caused harm in the world, like I’d somehow triggered wars or suicides just by making them. It didn’t feel like a thought I could argue with; it felt like a fact, and it crushed me. I stopped taking jobs, missed deadlines, barely saw my kids.

But the weirder stuff started before that and never really went away, even when my mood briefly lifts. I’m convinced there’s something rotting inside me, like my organs are decaying, even though tests come back normal. I sometimes see shadowy figures in my apartment or on set — people standing in doorways who vanish when I look twice. Those visions and the feeling my body is ruined are there regardless of whether I’m in that really low, crying state or not.

D015-D005_h025.question:
For the last 8 months or so, I’ve been really down most of the time. It’s like this heavy, gray mood that just doesn’t lift. I drag myself to the branch, but even there I feel like I’m failing at everything, like I’m useless and shouldn’t be in charge of anyone’s money. I’ve been eating a lot more—snacking late at night after these awful dreams—and I’ve put on quite a bit of weight over a few weeks, enough that my suits don’t fit properly.

The nightmares are constant—disturbing, vivid ones that jerk me awake in the early hours. I wake up sweaty, heart racing, and then lie there tasting this strange, metallic or bitter flavor in my mouth, like something’s been put there, even though there’s nothing.

On top of that, for more than a year now, I’ve had this unshakeable sense that one of my senior clients, a woman, is secretly in love with me. I “see” messages in how she signs her name or the way she looks at me, even though my wife insists I’m imagining it. That belief and the weird taste sensations were there before I got this low, and they haven’t gone away even on the rare days when my mood feels a bit lighter.

    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
